blind_spots.blind_spot: The SBIR abstract promises an Edge AI platform for DAF space/UAV imagery in 'dynamic warfighting environments,' but the company's live product today is a cloud-hosted maritime dashboard (plain email/password login, 'Sign in with Google') with no edge-deployment story anywhere.
blind_spots.operator_reality: If the edge-hardened, contested-environment capability from the Phase II never shipped, the company has effectively abandoned the fielding step — exactly the valley-of-death failure the EDP describes, now visible as a full product pivot rather than a stalled contract.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Small team (4-5 people) likely couldn't sustain both the DAF edge-deployment engineering and a commercial GTM motion, and chose the commercial path.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Global persistent awareness is critical for Department of Air Force (DAF) missions to win in dynamic warfighting environments

blind_spots.blind_spot: MaritimeIQ's flagship claim is tracking vessels 'even when they go dark' by fusing AIS, satellite, and RF data — real denied/degraded-signal engineering — but this DDIL-relevant capability is applied entirely to civilian shipping compliance, not reapplied to the DAF mission the SBIR funded.
blind_spots.operator_reality: The company clearly has the technical DNA for contested-environment sensor fusion; none of that expertise is visible in a warfighter-facing offering, suggesting the DoD-relevant engineering was set aside when the commercial pivot happened.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: GTM and revenue pressure likely drove the team toward the market (commercial maritime) where deals close faster than a DoD Phase III transition.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Track vessels in real time—even when they go dark. AIS spoofing? No problem.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Neither the commercial site nor the SBIR abstract mentions ITAR or export control, despite the SBIR covering space domain awareness/UAV imagery — a classically ITAR-sensitive area — and the live product ingesting satellite imagery with 'no speed or size limits.'
blind_spots.operator_reality: A team that built a DAF-funded imagery platform without a visible ITAR/export-control posture is the kind of company that discovers the compliance gate only when a program office asks for it — often too late to save the transition.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Team is optics/AI-first, not compliance-first, and the current commercial focus removes any pressure to surface it.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: High-res data from Sentinel and more

opener_hook: Misram's AF Phase II SBIR ($1.25M, 2023) for a DAF Edge AI space/UAV imagery platform is public — the company's live product today is an unrelated commercial maritime-tracking dashboard with no edge-deployment story.
what_they_do: Originally built an Edge AI platform for DAF space/UAV imagery intelligence under an AF SBIR Phase II; now operates MaritimeIQ, a commercial AI-powered maritime vessel-tracking and sanctions-compliance SaaS product, with no visible defense-facing product today.
